header.userPrompt:
Implement the plan in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-07-built-in-flows.md`, which implements the spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-built-in-flows-design.md`. Read both in full before planning.

Planning:
- Use the plan's 11 tasks as the run's tasks, in the same order, one run task per plan task. Do not merge, split or reorder them: later tasks depend on the exact signatures earlier tasks produce (each task's "Interfaces" block).
- Each task's description must name its plan task ("Task N: <title>") and tell the implementer to follow that section's steps and code, the plan's "Global Constraints", and the spec.

Implementation:
- The plan's code is the intended design. Deviate only when it does not compile or a test shows it is wrong, and then keep the deviation minimal and consistent with the spec and with the interfaces later tasks rely on.
- Ignore the plan's "Do NOT commit" constraint and the superpowers sub-skill line: this flow commits after each task.
- Before writing or reviewing Scala, invoke the `direct-style-scala` skill.
- Follow `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` for conventions and build/test commands. Run `sbt --client scalafmtAll` before finishing each task.
- Each task ends with the build compiling with zero warnings and the tests named in that task passing. Task 11 ends with a full `sbt test` passing.
- Do not edit history docs (ADRs other than the 0018 amendment, `docs/research/`, `docs/plans/`, `docs/superpowers/`).

Review: check each task against its plan section, the spec, and the plan's "Review Focus" list.

resultJson.description:
Reshape the shipped flow set to `quick.sc`, `implement.sc`, `epic.sc`, `resolve.sc` and `review.sc`, removing `simple.sc`, `implement-enhanced.sc`, `implement-interactive.sc`, `issue-pr.sc`, `issue-pr-bugfix.sc` and `examples/runnable/02-interactive/`. The flows become short, forkable examples: everything generic (reviewer picking, review prompt assembly, report rendering, PR-handle resolution, triage decoding, epic prompts) moves into the library so each script shows only its own stage sequence and decisions.

The library grows what the flows need: a resume-safe stage base commit recorded in the progress log (`stageStarts`), so a per-epic review after a mid-epic crash still covers the nested commits; `orca.plan.Roadmap` / `Epic` with `Plan.{autonomous,interactive}.roadmap` and `.reviewed()`; one `Triage` (`Reject` / `Accept(summary, brief, kind)` with `TestableBug` / `UntestableBug` / `Change`) replacing `assessThenPlan`, `Verdict` and `AssessedPlan`; `orca.review.reviewOnce` with `ReviewTarget` / `ReviewReport`; and `GitHubTool#prHandle`. `Plan.epicId` becomes `Plan.id`. Docs, the shell's test pins on the flow set, the authoring examples and an AGENTS.md "Built-in flows" guideline follow.

The design is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-built-in-flows-design.md`; the step-by-step plan with the intended code is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-07-built-in-flows.md`. The plan's code is the design: deviate only where it does not compile or a test shows it wrong, minimally, keeping the per-task "Interfaces" blocks intact since later tasks build on them. Unlike the plan's "Do NOT commit" line, this flow commits after every task.

resultJson.brief:
## Where things are

Read first: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-built-in-flows-design.md` (design) and `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-07-built-in-flows.md` (per-task steps and code; its "Global Constraints", "Review Focus", "File Structure" sections apply to every task). Then `AGENTS.md` (conventions, capability tokens, comment style, vocabulary) and `.orca/reviewers/orca.md` (the repo's own review rules). `CONTRIBUTING.md` has build/test commands.

Modules: `tools/` (git/gh tools, `orca.agents` LLM SPI, `InStage`/`WorkspaceWrite`, `orca.Par`, `orca.gitref`), `flow/` (`stage`/`display`/`fail`, `FlowContext`/`FlowControl`, `orca.{plan,review,pr,progress}`), `runner/` (`flow()` entry, `exports.scala`, `FlowCompilesTest`), `shell/` (`orca` CLI; bundles `flows/*.sc` as resources and pins the set in `BuiltInFlowsTest`), `flows/*.sc` (scala-cli scripts, outside scalafmt scope, pinned dep `org.virtuslab::orca:0.1.10`).

## Build and test

- Invoke the `direct-style-scala` skill before writing or reviewing Scala.
- Prefer plain `sbt "flow/testOnly ..."` in non-interactive shells (AGENTS.md warns `sbt --client` can attach to a stale server on the wrong JDK); the user asked for `sbt --client scalafmtAll` after each task, so run that, falling back to `sbt scalafmtAll` if the client fails. Never run `clean`. sbt runs take minutes; run them in the foreground and wait.
- Warnings enabled: `-Wunused:all -Wvalue-discard -Wnonunit-statement`; every task ends with zero warnings. Discard with `val _ = ...`. `@unused` on an unused `using` param (see `Plan.autonomousResult`).
- Tests: munit, one scenario per test. Fakes: `orca.testkit` (`TestAgent`, `ScriptedBackend`, `StubGitHubTool`, `GitRepo`, `TempDirs`, `branchName`), `TestFlowContext(dispatcher, userPrompt, workDir, stackSettings, reviewerCatalog, lead, wiredGit, wiredGh)`, `TestRun.create(dispatcher, userPrompt, lead, ...)` (fresh seeded git repo, progress header already written; `import run.given` for `FlowContext`+`FlowControl`; `run.control.stageBaseCommit`, `run.control.progressStore`, `run.context.git`). `InStage.unsafe` / `WorkspaceWrite.unsafe` only in tests.
- Integration compile of the flows: `ORCA_INTEGRATION=1 sbt publishLocal "shell/testOnly *BuiltInFlowsCompileTest"` (needs `scala-cli`; run it for Tasks 8–10).

## Conventions that bite here

- Braceless syntax, explicit return types on public members. No default values on `JsonData`/persisted case-class fields (`StageStart`, `Roadmap`, `TriageReply`, `ReviewTarget`...). No back-compat machinery; the progress-log shape may change freely.
- Comments: present-tense facts only, no history ("renamed from", "no longer"), no plan/task labels, no Scala mechanics; in `flows/*.sc` only facts about that file. Scaladoc = contract; `//` = implementation why.
- Vocabulary: `finding` (never `issue` for a review finding; `issue` = GitHub issue), `run`/`attempt`, plan `task`. Flow fix-turn caps are spelled out: per-task/per-epic loops `maxFixTurns = 3` (= `DefaultMaxFixTurns`, `ReviewLoop.scala:48`), every `"Final review"` loop `maxFixTurns = 5`, pinned by `BuiltInFlowsTest`.
